correctness.rationale: With u=cx and p=uy, multiplication of the two updates gives p'−1=(p−1)(1+p/(1+y²)). Hence the sign classes and the invariant equality are exact. Below the curve, if y were unbounded, the decrease in p for y≥1 would be at least (1−p₀)/2 times the increment in log y, contradicting bounded p. For finite limit Y, uₙ is bounded by u₀qⁿ, with q=Y²/(1+Y²); summability of log(q(yₙ)/q) gives the positive limiting prefactor and summing uₙ gives the stated tail for Y−yₙ. On the curve sₙ=yₙ² obeys Δsₙ=2+1/sₙ. First sₙ=2n+O(log n), then Δ(sₙ−2n−log(n)/2)=O(log(n)/n²), giving the constant and error. Above the curve, Δ(y²)≥2p₀, so y grows without bound. If u had zero limit, its telescoping decrement sum is a left Riemann sum for ∫ from yₙ to ∞ of (1+t²)⁻¹, with error at most uₙ/(1+yₙ²); this forces pₙ→1, impossible. For v=lim uₙ>0, yₙ/n→v and summing the same decrements first gives uₙ−v=O(1/n), then yₙ=vn+O(log n). The summand is consequently 1/(vk²)+O(log(k)/k³); summing it and then subtracting the harmonic drift from y proves both displayed errors. Strict y-increase excludes periodic orbits. value.rationale: For an existing dynamical family at an equilibrium-line parameter, local stability does not answer which positive initial states converge to that line and which escape. The explicit all-state separator answers that question without shooting or asymptotic parameter fitting and identifies a distinct critical motion, with quantitative convergence and scattering on its two sides. Even relative to the nearby parabolic model the endpoint's exact basin test is substantive.
